dedupe_keys.name: cook county administration building fire chicago 2003 occupant evacuation behaviour study

description: This case study documents how occupants behaved during the fire of 17 October 2003 in the 36-storey Cook County Administration Building in Chicago, which killed six people and injured about a dozen. It was produced by Guylène Proulx and colleagues at the National Research Council Canada's Institute for Research in Construction and published in April 2004 as a 92-page research report, free to download online as a PDF from the NRC Publications Archive. The study mailed a survey to all building occupants on their training and fire safety experience and, for those present, their actions during the fire; of 1,862 surveys, 551 were returned, including 89 from people in the building. Coverage is one building and event. Caveats: responses are self-reported months after the fire, and only about 250 people were inside at the time. The study found that although 85 percent had fire safety training, only about 20 percent knew the staged evacuation plan, 48 percent did not know stairwell doors would lock behind them, and half of those present used elevators; it identifies the evacuation announcements, locked stairwell doors and firefighting activity as combining to cause the deaths. Simulation uses: pre-evacuation and route choice parameters for building evacuation and emergency response models. Related records: the evacuation route choice experiment (data-evacuation-route-choice-web-experiment) gives experimental behaviour data.
